headline: Recommended appointment and ordinance change on Rogers Street parking, continued shopping cart ordinance to October 19, 2026
summary: The committee recommended appointing Philip Schwarz to the Open Space & Recreation Advisory Committee. It continued discussion of a proposed shopping cart ordinance to the October 19, 2026 meeting. It also recommended amending parking and tow-away zone rules on Rogers Street, with a public hearing set for September 22, 2026.
decisions: Recommended that the City Council appoint Philip Schwarz to the Open Space & Recreation Advisory Committee, TTE 2/15/2027, by a vote of 3 in favor, 0 opposed.
Continued CC#2026-017 (Benson) on shopping cart regulations to the October 19, 2026 Ordinance & Administration meeting.
Recommended that the City Council amend Chapter 22 Sections 22-270 and 22-291 regarding parking and tow-away zones on Rogers Street, by a vote of 3 in favor, 0 opposed.

O&A Committee September 14, 2026 Page 1 of 2
Ordinances & Administration Committee
Monday, September 14, 2026 – 6:00 p.m.
1st Floor Council Conference Room
9 Dale Avenue
Gloucester, MA 01930
-Minutes-
Present: Chair, Councilor Sean Nolan; Vice Chair, Councilor Frank Margiotta; Councilor Marjorie 
Grace
Other Councilors Present: Councilor Tony Gross; Councilor Dylan Benson
This meeting was conducted in-person and remotely via ZOOM.
The meeting was called to order at 6:00 p.m.
1. Boards, Committees, and Commissions
New Appointments
Open Space & Recreation Advisory Committee   Philip Schwarz (fulfilling unexpired term)     TTE 2/15/2027
Summary of Discussion: Philip Schwarz stated that he was a part of the Cape Ann Trail Stewards, and 
was currently serving as board president. He stated that he had a long-standing interest in the area of 
Dogtown. He stated he was looking forward to working with the Committee. 
The committee thanked Philip Schwarz for his willingness to volunteer his time.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Margiotta, seconded by Councilor Grace,
the Ordinances & Administration Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council
appoint Philip Schwarz to the Open Space & Recreation Advisory Committee, TTE 2/15/2027.
2. CC#2026-017 (Benson): Amend GCO Ch. 14 “Offenses and Miscellaneous Provisions” by 
ADDING a new Article IV “Shopping Cart Regulations,” Sec. 14-46 “Definitions,” Sec. 14-47 
“Identification of shopping carts,” Sec. 14-48 “Shopping carts to be confined to premises,” Sec. 
14-49 “Enforcement.”
Summary of Discussion: Councilor Benson stated that an ongoing issue that had been brought to him by
constituents was that shopping carts were being found around different areas of the downtown. 
Councilor Nolan stated that he wanted there to be outreach to businesses before the matter was voted on. He
stated that he supported the changes to the proposed ordinance amendment.
Councilor Benson stated he could reach out to the various businesses with shopping carts about the proposed
ordinance amendment over the next month.
This matter was continued to the October 19, 2026 Ordinance & Administration meeting.
O&A Committee September 14, 2026 Page 2 of 2
3. CC#2026-020 (Gross): Amend GCO Ch. 22 “Traffic and Motor Vehicles,” Sec. 22-270 “Parking 
prohibited at all times” and Sec. 22-291 “Tow-away Zones” re: Rogers Street.
Summary of Discussion: Councilor Gross stated that the proposed ordinance amendment came after a
meeting with businesses and Senator Tarr and Representative Tarr and the City. He stated that the only
parking that would be eliminated would be Gorton’s personnel parking. He stated that there had been several
near misses of cars hitting pedestrians. He stated that there would be a traffic safety study on the area as well.
Councilor Benson asked if it was Gorton’s that was asking for the proposed changes. Councilor Gross stated
that it was. He stated it would not affect trailer truck parking.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grace, seconded by Councilor 
Margiotta, the Ordinances & Administration Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the
City Council amend the Gloucester Code of Ordinances, Chapter 22 “Traffic and Motor Vehicles” as 
follows: 
Amend Section 22-270 “Parking prohibited at all times” and Section 22-291 “Tow-away Zones” by
